title: Check the detail the idea turns on
statement: Aim each check at what the page is for: the detail the lesson's idea or theme turns on, never an incidental detail nothing depends on.
example: A spot-check of four lessons found two checks about incidental details.
detail: In one lesson, the reading check on the part holding the line the theme of betrayal turns on asked about a gold coin instead, so that detail went unchecked until the modelling moment; the check was then reworded to it (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd`). A spot-check of four other lessons asked whether each part-check was about the thematic hinge, not an incidental detail: most landed on the same hinge as their part's purpose line, and two checks in one lesson were incidental rather than thematic (the same file). What the page is for also covers the causes and effects the lesson builds on later and the goals it states.
against: Whether a literal reading check must also be about the hinge was still awaiting a ruling, so the two incidental checks were not changed (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd`). On the audited lesson one sequence check was left in place, since no harm was shown (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, line 113). Fixing the project's own two checks was held pending a ruling on whether checks that stay literal must also be about the hinge (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd`, lines 64-66).
